paper_metadata.title: Evaluation of High-Vacuum Annealing and Hot Isostatic Pressing on the Microstructure and Properties of an Additively Manufactured Niobium Alloy

evidence.quote: Niobium alloy C-103 is a refractory alloy historically used in the manufacturing and design of high-temperature aerospace propulsion components. C-103 consists of niobium alloyed with 10 wt.% hafnium, and 1 wt.% titanium (Nb-10Hf-1Ti).

The chemical compositions of the powder and manufactured specimens were determined using two methods depending on the elements of interest. The Nb, Hf, Ti, W, and Zr contents were measured using inductively coupled plasma–mass spectrometry, while the O, N, and C contents were measured using a LECO series 836 combustion analyzer.

A set of printed specimens was subjected to HIP. During HIP, specimens were individually wrapped in Ta foil to prevent oxidation and were loaded into a high-pressure inert-gas environment and held at a temperature of 1500 °C.

parameters.cooling_method: cooled to ambient under vacuum overnight

evidence.quote: For each heat treatment, the specimens were brought to a vacuum of 10 /C06 torr and heated from room temperature to the target temperature at a rate of 17/C176C/min. After the desired temperature was reached and sustained for 1 h, the heater was turned off and the setup allowed to cool to ambient conditions under vacuum overnight.
